subject: Comparing different classification schemes in BioGeoBEARS

messages.author: 4e79cae74d18635e
messages.subject: Comparing different classification schemes in BioGeoBEARS
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am studying mouse lemur diversification in Madagascar. We use BioGeoBEARS to reconstruct ancestral ranges/habitats for the genus. A variety of different habitat classifications exists for Madagascar, ranging from binary (humid/dry) to more fine-scale ones that distinguish a higher number of ecosystem types. We reconstructed ancestral habitats for many of them but, ideally, we would also like to test which of theses classifications explains mouse lemur diversification best. Is there a way to compare modelling results from analyses with different classifications (e.g., humid/dry vs. one using more tip states such as humid/subhumid/dry)? These classifications are not necessarily nested.

Can the AIC (weights) be used for this? I am unsure because a different classification is not a model change but a change in input data... I searched the google group for an answer to this issue but could only find the following rather old entry, which did not resolve the issue: https://groups.google.com/g/biogeobears/c/Jlab5WketCo

Cheers,
Tobias
